correctness.rationale: The theorem specifies all positivity and bath-normalization assumptions and derives the stationary heat current from a uniquely stable pinned Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process. The 2-by-4 cross-covariance solves eight exact linear equations with determinant 4D/m^2. Symbolic elimination gives the rational conductance and the global inverse-conductance square, whose only zero is the claimed positive central mass. An independently constructed complete 6-by-6 covariance solution for eight positive rational parameter sets confirms the same heat current; this is a check rather than an infinite-domain proof.

value.rationale: The middle mass is a natural design parameter controlling spectral matching in a minimal anchored harmonic conductor. The theorem supplies a complete unconstrained positive-mass optimization for all pinning/friction values, a surprising universal friction-independent optimum, a strict improvement over uniform masses for every positive pinning, and an exact positive-square mismatch penalty. These distinguish it from textbook energy-balance identities and arbitrary numerical samples even though the underlying Green-function transport framework is established.
